title: Robust Latent-Drift Compensation with FTM Anchoring (Section 3.5 reference implementation)
description: Single-file C++17 reference implementation of Section 3.5 (drift compensation and FTM anchoring of the radiomap) of a dissertation on hybrid Bayesian tactical spatial identification of Wi-Fi signal sources. A low-dimensional latent-drift overlay is estimated by a Kalman predict/update (eq. 3.16-3.18) with a component-wise Huber robust influence function (eq. 3.19), while the approved base radiomap stays immutable (Figure 3.6). A trusted-update gate (eq. 3.20) separates quarantine from update, and the next FTM responder is chosen by expected information gain (eq. 3.21). The Kalman gain is computed by a stable Cholesky solve (no explicit matrix inverse); suppressed residuals are retained as anomaly evidence; coordinate uncertainty is propagated into the innovation covariance. The demonstration injects a spoofed RSSI (Huber rejects it) and an unverified-incident gate closure (quarantine). No external dependencies; runs as-is on OnlineGDB. Operating points are to_be_validated. Analytical illustration, not empirical data.
